 Marvel Star Speaks Out on Getting Recast for MCU Reboot
 in Entertainment , Marvel 
 Posted on November 5, 2026 by Thomas Hitchen 
 Leave a comment 
 Credit: Gage Skidmore, Flickr
 Marvel Studios has officially found its next Ghost Rider, and the actor who last carried the flaming chain on the big screen has finally weighed in.
 Credit: Marvel Studios 
 Ryan Gosling (Johnny Blaze/Ghost Rider) was confirmed as the Marvel Cinematic Universe’s new Spirit of Vengeance at San Diego Comic-Con in July 2026 , ending years of speculation over when the character would make his proper MCU debut. Now, Nicolas Cage, who played Johnny Blaze in two Sony Marvel films released outside the MCU, has addressed the studio’s decision, and his response could hardly be more gracious.
 Original Ghost Rider Speaks Out
 Speaking to The Hollywood Reporter on the red carpet for the premiere of his new movie, Madden (2026), Cage made it clear that he holds no resentment about another actor taking over the role. Instead, he welcomed the chance for someone new to interpret Johnny Blaze in this recast MCU reboot.
 “Ryan’s going to do his thing with it, and I’m looking forward to seeing it,” Cage told The Hollywood Reporter . The actor also revealed that the pair have stayed on good terms away from the cameras, adding: “Ryan knows how I feel about him as an actor; we’ve had nice conversations, and we stay in touch.”
 Cage reiterated his enthusiasm for Gosling taking on the character and wished his successor well. His comments suggest the handover has been an amicable one, rather than a contentious recasting.
 Credit: Sony Pictures 
 Ryan Gosling’s Casting Has Been Years in the Making
 Marvel Studios made the announcement official during its Hall H presentation at San Diego Comic-Con on July 25, 2026, when Marvel Studios President Kevin Feige introduced Gosling as the star of a new standalone Ghost Rider movie.
 For those who have followed Gosling’s career, the news did not arrive entirely out of nowhere. In 2022, the actor told journalist Josh Horowitz that Ghost Rider was the Marvel character he most wanted to portray. Horowitz subsequently raised the idea with Feige, who expressed interest in finding a place for Gosling in the MCU.
 Feige referenced that earlier conversation before bringing Gosling onto the stage, and the actor confirmed that discussions had taken place behind the scenes. Asked what drew him to the role, Gosling offered a simple explanation: “Just a feeling.”
 Credit: Gage Skidmore, Flickr 
 Shawn Levy Will Direct Marvel’s New Ghost Rider Movie
 Marvel has tapped Shawn Levy ( Deadpool & Wolverine ) to direct. Levy and Gosling have already established a working relationship through Star Wars: Starfighter (2027) , and the two reportedly began discussing Ghost Rider while collaborating on the Lucasfilm project. Levy recalled eventually telling Gosling: “Bro, let’s ride.”
 Levy is no stranger to the MCU either, having previously directed the billion-dollar hit Deadpool & Wolverine (2024). The pairing of Gosling and Levy signals a fresh creative direction for the franchise.
 Nicolas Cage’s History as Johnny Blaze
 Cage remains the actor most closely associated with Johnny Blaze’s live-action big-screen appearances. He first played the character in Ghost Rider (2007), directed by Mark Steven Johnson, before returning in Ghost Rider: Spirit of Vengeance (2012), which followed Blaze as he attempted to protect a child from the Devil.
 Credit: Sony Pictures 
 Both films received mixed critical responses, but Cage’s interpretation remains an important part of the character’s live-action history. Marvel later explored another version of the character through Gabriel Luna (Robbie Reyes/Ghost Rider) in Agents of S.H.I.E.L.D. , while Cage was reportedly considered for a cameo in Deadpool & Wolverine before ultimately not appearing.
 Gosling’s casting therefore represents a new interpretation of Johnny Blaze, rather than a continuation of Cage’s original franchise.
 What We Know About Marvel’s Ghost Rider Movie
 The standalone film is currently targeting a July 28, 2028, theatrical release, which would place it a couple of months behind the projected release of the recently confirmed X-Men movie . Supporting cast announcements remain limited, though Connor Storrie has been linked to the project in an undisclosed role, and Sacha Baron Cohen (Mephisto) is expected to reprise his role following his appearance in Ironheart .
 Marvel casting director Sarah Finn has described (via Comic Book Movie ) Gosling as “the perfect choice” for the character.
 Credit: Marvel Studios 
 Could Nicolas Cage Still Return to the MCU?
 Cage’s comments do not necessarily rule out a future appearance. Speculation has surrounded a possible Ghost Rider appearance in Avengers: Secret Wars (2027), although other rumors suggest Gosling could appear in the crossover instead . Marvel has not confirmed whether Cage will return in any capacity.
 For fans, Cage’s blessing removes any awkwardness from the transition. By the time Gosling’s film arrives in 2028, 16 years will have passed since Johnny Blaze last led a movie, and Marvel now has the chance to give Ghost Rider a fresh cinematic identity while honoring the legacy Cage established. For now, Cage appears content to pass the torch, and the wait for Gosling’s ride begins.
 How do you feel about Ryan Gosling’s casting as Ghost Rider in the MCU? Let Inside the Magic know in the comments below!

 Thomas Hitchen 
 When he’s not thinking about the Magic Kingdom, Thomas is usually reading a book, becoming desperately obsessed with fictional characters, or baking something delicious (his favorite is chocolate cake -- to bake and to eat). He's a dreamer and grew up on Mulan saving the world, Jim Hawkins soaring through the stars, and Padmé Amidala fighting a Nexu. At the Parks, he loves to ride Everest, stroll down Main Street with an overstuffed pin lanyard around his neck, and eat as many Mickey-shaped ice creams as possible. His favorite character is Han Solo (yes, he did shoot first), and his favorite TV show is Buffy the Vampire Slayer except when it's One Tree Hill. He loves sandy beach walks, forest hikes, and foodie days out in the Big City.
Thomas lives in England, UK, with his fiancée, baby, and their dog, a Border Collie called Luna.
